title: Phased Helix deployment for cost recommendation activation
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Implement a conservative, observable, and operator-friendly activation lifecycle for batching/caching recommendations produced by Optimize. We call the pattern 'Phased Helix' — a ratcheted, multi-stage activation flow that combines shadow validation, micro-canaries, rolling activation windows, operator checkpoints, and automatic rollback triggers.

Scope:
- Automate safe application of Optimize suggestions to hosted and Dedicated model routes.
- Provide a deterministic canary policy (micro-canaries + staggered percentage ramp).
- Expose an operator approval path and optional human-in-the-loop pauses.
- Strong telemetry: per-tenant latency, p50/p95 token cost delta, error spikes, hallucination/regression signals from eval hooks.

Out of scope for this ticket: Private on-prem installer changes (will follow in ENG-XXX), full RBAC UI overhaul.

Acceptance criteria:
- Admin API to create a Phased Helix activation bundle that declares: suggestion id, target routes, canary schedule, safety thresholds, and approval requirement.
- Canary runner that can run shadow traffic and then small-percentage live traffic increments with rollback thresholds enforced automatically.
- Operator console (Console) shows live canary progress, key telemetry, and a single-click abort/approve.
- Playbook + automated revert within 5 minutes of threshold breach.
- End-to-end automated tests and a chaos test that simulates degraded model responses/latency and verifies rollback behavior.

Design notes / decisions:
- Use existing rollout engine as orchestration backbone but place a safety shim (policy-evaluator) in front of final commit.
- Shadow validation (100% traffic mirrored) will run first for 1 hour for any non-trivial suggestion; metric deltas must be within configured thresholds before live canary.
- Default canary progression: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 30% -> 100% with configurable dwell times. Micro-canaries (0.5%) are prioritized to detect regressions on small but representative traffic.
- Telemetry signals: latency tail (p99), token-per-response delta, model-quality metric (eval-f1/regression score), and error-rate. Threshold breach on any critical signal triggers automatic rollback and operator notification.
- Rollback strategy: immediate config revert + short circuit to prior model variant for existing inflight requests; postmortem ticket generated automatically.

Trade-offs:
- Conservative defaults increase time to realize cost savings but limit risk exposure.
- Shadow validation increases compute cost — acceptable trade given high impact of regressing customer-facing quality.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Schema additions: activation bundle + canary plan (API & DB).
2) Policy evaluator service: threshold checks, runbook integrations, simulated traffic harness.
3) Canary runner: orchestrates traffic percentages, monitors metrics, invokes rollback.
4) Console integration: progress UI, approval modal, abort button.
5) Tests: unit, integration, end-to-end canary simulation, and chaos scenarios.

Safety review required: true
